title: SmolLM3-3B model card
notes: The card for the one model in this dataset that Hugging Face created rather than hosted. "SmolLM3 is a 3B parameter language model designed to push the boundaries of small models. It supports dual mode reasoning, 6 languages and long context. SmolLM3 is a fully open model that offers strong performance at the 3B–4B scale." Front matter states "license: apache-2.0". On context, the card states one figure for the shipped configuration and larger ones the operator has to enable, and these are not rival claims. Its long-context section reads: "The current `config.json` is set for context length up to 65,536 tokens. To handle longer inputs (128k or 256k), we utilize YaRN you can change the `max_position_embeddings` and rope_scaling` to:" — the run-on and the unpaired backtick after rope_scaling are the card's own — followed by a config block carrying ""original_max_position_embeddings": 65536," and a "yarn" rope_scaling type with a factor of 2.0, which the block's inline comment applies to 65,536 to reach the 128k figure. The feature bullet states that same relationship rather than contradicting it: "Trained on 64k context and supports up to **128k tokens** using YARN extrapolation"; reading its "64k" as the 65,536 the config names is an inference from the usual binary sense of k rather than something the card spells out. The recorded contextWindow is 65536 because that is the only figure the card presents as the setting the model ships with, while 128k and 256k are reachable only once the operator edits max_position_embeddings and rope_scaling, which makes them properties of a changed configuration. That the same sentence offers 256k on the same footing as 128k is what settles it: were 128k a competing account of the shipped window, 256k would be one too, and nothing would recommend recording 256k. The long-context benchmark rows also report a "Ruler 128k" score for SmolLM3-3B, and the card does not state whether YaRN was applied to obtain it; an evaluation result is not a statement of the shipped configuration either way. On languages, the card names six as native: "- **Multilingual**: 6 natively supported (English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, and Portuguese)". Its front matter "language:" list has eight entries — en, fr, es, it, pt, zh, ar, ru — and the three of those that are not among the six are accounted for by the card itself rather than contradicting it: "The model has also been trained on Arabic (standard), Chinese and Russian data, but has seen fewer tokens in these languages compared to the 6 above. We report the performance on these langages for information." (the misspelling of "languages" is the card's own), and the benchmark tables carry a section headed "| Other supported languages |" covering exactly Arabic, Chinese and Russian. So the front matter is those six native languages plus these three secondary ones, less one: it carries no "- de" entry, while the prose counts German among the six and the "| Main supported languages |" table reports a "| German| MLMM Hellaswag |" row. That single omission is the whole of the discrepancy — a gap in the front matter, not a disagreement about what the model supports. No language fact is recorded for this release, and not because of that gap: the release schema has no field for natural-language coverage, so there is nowhere to record one.
